summary.headline: JSW Infrastructure Q1 FY27 operating EBITDA rose 16% YoY to INR674 crores on 31 MT cargo; FY27 volume guided to 127 MT excluding Fujairah.
summary.overview: Consolidated operating revenue rose 18% YoY to INR1,445 crores and operating EBITDA rose 16% to INR674 crores, while PAT fell to INR358 crores from INR390 crores on lower other income and higher tax rate. Cargo volume grew 6% YoY to 31 MT, with India operations up 11% excluding Fujairah, which contributed negligibly due to the Middle East environment. The company completed a INR7,503 crore QIP, reporting a net cash position of INR2,769 crores as of June 2026, and Moody's upgraded the rating to Baa3. Management reaffirmed FY27 operating EBITDA guidance of about INR3,000 crores and FY28 of INR5,000 crores.

segments.name: Ports
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,208 crores (+11% YoY) and EBITDA INR601 crores (+7%), margin 49.8% vs 51.8%; Jaigarh drove the sequential improvement, with Fujairah's drag estimated at INR65-70 crores of EBITDA in the quarter.

segments.name: Logistics (incl. Navkar and rakes)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR237 crores and EBITDA INR73 crores, margin 30.6%; Navkar revenue INR191 crores (+38%), EBITDA INR33 crores (+62%), PAT INR12 crores vs INR2 crores; domestic cargo 385,000 t (+40%), EXIM 83,000 TEUs (+2%).

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating EBITDA guidance of approximately INR3,000 crores reaffirmed; FY28 operating EBITDA guidance of INR5,000 crores reaffirmed.
FY27 cargo volume guided to around 127 MT, which excludes Fujairah; Fujairah is expected to add about 2-2.5 MT and INR100-125 crores of EBITDA in FY27.
Capacity target raised to 300 MTPA by FY28 and 400 MTPA by FY30 or earlier from current 186 MTPA.
Fleet target of about 250 rakes (around 110 rail and 140 container) over 2-3 years; the 40 rakes ordered in April 2026 expected by January-February 2027, taking the fleet to 80+ from 42.
FY27-FY28 capex plan of about INR16,500 crores (INR13,000 crores ports, INR3,500 crores logistics); INR5,500 crores already committed.
capex_capacity: Cumulative capex of about INR6,900 crores up to June 2026, including INR671 crores spent in Q1 FY27.
Slurry pipeline: 251 km lowered (about 83% complete), on track for March 2027 completion.
Murbe (Maharashtra): environmental clearance received and DFC rail connectivity approved; concession agreement expected in 2-3 months, construction to start around December 2026-January 2027.
Keni port: application at Karnataka CZMA; expected MoEF&CC clearance in about 3-4 months; FY30 timeline noted as deferred by about a year.

Kolkata (Netaji Subhas Dock) PPP award lifts capacity to about 1.4 million TEUs; capex about INR740 crores; Phase 1 (Berths 7-8) steady-state EBITDA about INR70-90 crores; full project INR300-350 crores.

Mangalore container terminal expanded to 6 MTPA from 4.2 MTPA; South West Port Goa consent to operate at 12 MTPA from 11 MTPA; Tuticorin bulk terminal on schedule; Jaigarh and Dharamtar brownfield expansions progressing.
Jatadhar (Odisha) construction in full swing after novation with anchor customer; Oman port bid invited in June, concession expected in about 1-2 months.
demand_pricing: Volume growth of 6% overall and 11% excluding Fujairah; Jaigarh growth from anchor volumes and third-party newer cargo segments (alumina, project cargo, LPG).
Management said alumina and project cargo gains are one-time, though incremental LPG cargo is expected to continue.
Insurance claim on Fujairah filed; resolution expected by end-October 2026.
Fujairah: 8 tanks expected operational by end-July or early August 2026; three more tanks expected by September-October; ability to operate depends on market conditions.
Murbe catchment split of roughly 20% group and 80% third-party; Keni hinterland linked to Ballari-Hosapete mineral and metal industries.
Rake revenue mix about 75% third-party and 25% group at present; target 45-55 split across rakes.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of geopolitical cost escalation on under-construction projects such as the slurry pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no ongoing projects were affected; minor LPG and diesel availability issues were normal execution noise, and any escalation is absorbed in project contingency.

qa_highlights.question: How much extra EBITDA would Fujairah normal operations have added in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said port EBITDA would have been about INR670-675 crores, implying INR65-70 crores of incremental EBITDA, with INR8 crores of Fujairah expense already included.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the port margin improve sequentially and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Jaigarh drove it through alumina and project cargo, which management said is not recurring; one-time crane-shifting costs of INR8-9 crores were incurred, and SWPL and Dharamtar volume mix is seen as normal going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Keni deferred and what are the remaining execution risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the delay to the KCZMA not being constituted for 6-7 months; it expects land risks to be minimal as the projects are reclamation-based.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall sharply QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury balances fell due to equity funding of ongoing projects; QIP proceeds received by June 30 should lift treasury income for the rest of the year. Q4 FY26 included about INR40 crores of interest received from Hiranandani on Jaigarh JV receivables.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rake EBITDA margin of about 90%, and will it continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rake revenue of INR43 crores records only premium and rebate, with haulage netted off; margin would be about 25% if freight were included, and treatment varies by rake type (LSFTO, GPWIS, container).

risks_watch: Fujairah ramp-up depends on tank readiness (8 tanks by August, 3 more by Sept-Oct) and on market conditions; the insurance claim resolution is targeted for October 2026.
Keni clearance: MoEF&CC approval expected in 3-4 months, with the project deferred by about a year.
GPWIS rake moratorium could change the 250-rake fleet target, and the Navkar merger is undecided.
Murbe and Keni are greenfield ports competing with JNPT and Adani's Hazira; third-party volume ramp is unproven.
Other income and PBT are under pressure from capex funding until QIP proceeds are deployed; management also said Q1 port margin was helped by one-time mix and will normalise.
summary.management_tone: Confident on execution and guidance, with the FY27 EBITDA guide reaffirmed; cautious on Fujairah, where volumes are excluded from the 127 MT guidance and recovery timing is uncertain. Management was evasive on Navkar's merger ("We'll communicate at the right time").
key_quotes: Excluding Fujairah, our India operations recorded an impressive 11% year-on-year growth in cargo volumes, significantly outpacing overall industry growth and validating the strength of our business model and deep customer relationships.
We should deliver you a number of around 127 million tonnes this year.

Given the strong operating momentum and execution progress across ports and logistics, we reaffirm our operating EBITDA guidance of approximately INR3,000 crores for FY27 and INR5,000 crores for FY28.

growth.why: FY27 operating EBITDA ~INR3,000 crore and FY28 INR5,000 crore reaffirmed, with FY27 volume guided to ~127 MT ex-Fujairah and capacity rising from 186 to 300 MTPA by FY28; backing is partly specific (rakes ordered, Kolkata PPP, Goa/Mangalore consents, 90% utilisation) but the FY28 EBITDA jump relies on capacity not yet commissioned.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Port EBITDA margin fell to 49.8% from 51.8% YoY, with Fujairah dragging INR65-70 crores of EBITDA; Q1 was helped by one-time alumina and project cargo, so margin recovery depends on Fujairah ramp and normalisation of Jaigarh mix, while logistics margin rose to 30.6% from 14.5%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Utilisation is at 90%, 40 rakes take the fleet from 42 to 80+ by Jan-Feb 2027, Fujairah 8 tanks come by Aug 2026 and 3 more by Sep-Oct 2026, and the Kolkata PPP lifts capacity to about 1.4 million TEUs, though Keni is deferred about a year and Murbe construction only starts Dec 2026-Jan 2027.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 cargo guided to around 127 MT excluding Fujairah, against 31 MT in Q1 (+6% YoY, +11% ex-Fujairah), with Fujairah adding about 2-2.5 MT in FY27 if tanks come online; alumina and project cargo gains are one-time, so the run-rate needs LPG and new rakes to carry it.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27-FY28 capex plan is about INR16,500 crores with INR5,500 crores committed, utilisation is 90%, and Murbe concession agreement is expected within 2-3 months with construction from Dec 2026-Jan 2027.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 operating EBITDA of about INR3,000 crores was only reaffirmed, not raised, with Q1 port EBITDA at INR601 crores and Fujairah still excluded from volume guidance and dependent on market conditions.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Fujairah recovery depends on tank readiness and market conditions with the insurance claim due by end-October 2026, and FY28 EBITDA of INR5,000 crores relies on capacity not yet commissioned, while port margin normalises after one-time Q1 benefits.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Incremental LPG cargo is expected to continue and third-party rake and rail services are ramping, but no specific new product or service launch with a date was quantified on the call.

rows.label: Fleet expansion to 80+ rakes
rows.why: 40 rakes ordered in April 2026 are expected by Jan-Feb 2027, taking the fleet from 42 to 80+, with a ~250-rake target over 2-3 years.

rows.label: Oman port concession
rows.why: Oman port bid was invited in June 2026 with concession expected in about 1-2 months, but no award is confirmed yet.

rows.label: Keni MoEF&CC clearance
rows.why: Keni application is at Karnataka CZMA with MoEF&CC clearance expected in about 3-4 months, and the project is already deferred by about a year after KCZMA was not constituted for 6-7 months.

tone.note: Management was confident on the FY27 EBITDA guide, Murbe and Kolkata execution, and 90% utilisation, but cautious on Fujairah recovery, one-time Q1 port margin help, and evasive on the Navkar merger; analysts pushed on margin sustainability, Fujairah normal EBITDA, Keni deferral and rake margin.
